skills.name: backend-engineer
skills.description: Implement reliable server-side APIs and services with explicit validation, authorization, errors, persistence, observability, and compatibility. Use for backend behavior or API implementation.

skills.name: code-reviewer
skills.description: Review a diff for correctness, security, maintainability, regressions, performance, and missing tests, with findings tied to concrete evidence. Use for pull requests or pre-merge review.

skills.name: execution-grinder
skills.description: Persist through implementation blockers using bounded attempts, escalating diagnostics, explicit stop conditions, and honest evidence. Use when work is blocked or repeated approaches fail.

skills.name: frontend-engineer
skills.description: Implement accessible, responsive frontend behavior inside an existing component, routing, styling, and state system. Use for browser or client UI changes.

skills.name: git-workflow
skills.description: Perform safe, reviewable Git operations with focused history, branch awareness, conflict recovery, and remote verification. Use for commits, merges, releases, and pushes.

skills.name: idea-grinder
skills.description: Pressure-test a product, technical, or business idea with high-leverage questions, counterarguments, alternatives, evidence requirements, and a falsifiable experiment. Use before recommending implementation.

skills.name: planner
skills.description: Turn a request into an executable implementation plan with explicit scope, assumptions, dependencies, risks, acceptance checks, and a stopping condition. Use before non-trivial coding, migration, debugging, or release work.

skills.name: qa-engineer
skills.description: Design and execute risk-based quality checks across acceptance paths, boundaries, failures, compatibility, and regression surface. Use before delivery or when behavior confidence is low.

skills.name: repo-explorer
skills.description: Map an unfamiliar repository before implementation by tracing entry points, configuration, conventions, tests, ownership, and the smallest relevant runtime path. Use when repository context is missing or uncertain.

skills.name: requirements-checker
skills.description: Turn vague requests into testable requirements by finding missing actors, states, constraints, contradictions, and acceptance evidence. Use when a request could produce rework or unsafe interpretation.

skills.name: researcher
skills.description: Produce source-backed technical research by defining the question, prioritizing authoritative evidence, resolving contradictions, and separating fact from inference. Use for changing topics and decisions.

skills.name: security-reviewer
skills.description: Review a system or change for attack surface, trust boundaries, authorization, secrets, dependencies, abuse cases, and security evidence. Use for security-sensitive work or release review.

skills.name: simplify
skills.description: Reduce unnecessary complexity while preserving required behavior, safety, observability, and maintainability. Use when a design, implementation, or plan has speculative layers or duplication.

skills.name: skill-router
skills.description: Route a request to the smallest compatible set of skills and define dependencies, safe parallelism, hand-offs, permissions, and final verification. Use when work spans domains or stages.

skills.name: technical-writer
skills.description: Write accurate developer documentation from verified behavior, runnable examples, clear recovery paths, and explicit assumptions. Use for READMEs, API docs, runbooks, and release notes.

skills.name: workflow-coordinator
skills.description: Coordinate complete feature, bug-fix, research, security, documentation, release, and multi-agent workflows using bounded playbooks and accepted artifacts. Use when a request needs several dependent stages.
